title: Machine learning-assisted serum Raman spectroscopy for risk stratification in men with suspected prostate cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
summary: Supervised classifiers analyzed dried-serum Raman spectra from archived samples to distinguish prostate-cancer cases from symptomatic controls. The single-biobank proof of concept reported moderate discrimination and lacks external or prospective validation.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning classifiers of serum Raman spectra; XGBoost
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Among 119 cancer cases and 60 symptomatic controls, reported AUC was about 0.77 overall and 0.78 in the PSA 4–10 ng/mL subgroup.
evidence.unknown: Single-biobank retrospective samples; no external or prospective validation. The authors note that contemporary pathway validation is needed.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised machine-learning classifiers of serum Raman spectra; XGBoost

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
